profiles.name: Andrew Steven Faulkner
profiles.description: Andrew Steven Faulkner, 24, of Beaverton OR, charged July 6, 2020 with assaulting federal officers using high-intensity lasers during the July 5-6, 2020 Portland federal courthouse protests. Possessed a sheathed machete at arrest. Pleaded guilty; 6 months detention + 3 years probation + 40 hours community service.
profiles.finding: Official DOJ sentencing release matches case; six months was HOME detention, flag biography discrepancy for separate review. Blog composite requires original portrait verification; deceased soldier namesake excluded.

profiles.name: Rudy Alvarez
profiles.description: On July 2, 2020 Rudy Alvarez, 24, was charged with aiming a laser pointer at a San Diego Police Department aircraft during a Black Lives Matter protest. No prison time imposed; 5 years probation.
profiles.finding: San Diego appellate case matches; Boston classmate/Getty image not linked to defendant.

profiles.name: Isaiah Bryant
profiles.description: On June 30, 2020 Isaiah Bryant, 24, was arrested in Los Angeles, CA by the "Safe LA Task Force" after the George Floyd Protests. He was found guilty of looting; sentenced to 5 months county jail. Currently held at the 77th Division Jail on other charges.
profiles.finding: Florida, NC and Georgia arrests and athlete/soldier namesakes not linked to Los Angeles case; reject. Local targeted query no accepted image.

profiles.name: Jeremy J. Ryan
profiles.description: On June 26, 2020 Jeremy J. Ryan, 31, of Madison, WI was charged with making terrorist threats and stalking (both felonies) plus other misdemeanors for allegedly threatening to release personal information about Dane County Sheriff Dave Mahoney and his family and calling on protestors to harass Mahoney's family home. Sentenced to 3 months in Wisconsin state prison.
profiles.finding: Madison commercial review avatar not independently linked; reject pending stronger identity source.

profiles.name: Miguel Ramos
profiles.description: Miguel Ramos, 26, with Dyshika McFadden and Tindal, used an aerosol can and open flame to set fire to an RPD vehicle during the May 30, 2020 Rochester NY BLM protests. The burning was broadcast on Facebook Live. Convicted at trial; 16 months federal prison + $4,287 restitution.
profiles.finding: DOJ Rochester case matches, but states age21 in2022 unlike database26. SF fentanyl, Houston officer and historical namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Adrian Wood
profiles.description: Adrian Wood, 21, was charged with one count of civil disorder in Wilmington, DE. Wood threw a brick through the back window of an occupied Wilmington police cruiser during an evening of protests and looting in the city's downtown area. Sentenced to time served (~18.6 months between arrest June 15, 2020 and judgment January 3, 2022).
profiles.finding: Official Delaware complaint matches; Texas and British offender namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Ivan Jacob Zecher
profiles.description: On June 10, 2020 in Jacksonville, FL, Ivan Jacob Zecher, 27, was charged with felon in possession of a firearm and unlawful possession of an unregistered firearm. During a protest, a group blocking traffic was reportedly throwing rocks and water bottles at officers. Officers arrested Zecher; his backpack was leaking — they found a liquor bottle full of gasoline, a lighter, balloons full of liquid, and a hatchet. Case dropped (illegal arrest).
profiles.finding: DOJ complaint and indictment confirm Jacksonville identity; obituary relationship mention is not a portrait.

profiles.name: Jhajuan Sabb
profiles.description: Jhajuan Sabb, 20, of Troy NY, made several Facebook Live videos threatening to throw bricks at the Troy PD, Troy police vehicles, and Troy City Hall during the June 2020 BLM protests, and offered instructions for making firebombs. Pleaded guilty; 8 months federal prison + 3 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: WAMC reporting connects Troy threats and later Albany case; portrait lead remains uninspected.

profiles.name: Vincent Hamer
profiles.description: On June 3, 2020 Vincent Hamer, 18, was arrested in connection with vandalism at the Nashville Historic Courthouse. Police say video and photographs show Hamer using objects to break at least two windows at the courthouse on May 30, 2020 after a peaceful protest over George Floyd's death. Sentenced to 1.6 months in Tennessee state prison plus supervised probation.
profiles.finding: WDEF and Yahoo local sentencing report identify Nashville defendant, photo lead remains.

profiles.name: David Elmakayes
profiles.description:
David Elmakayes was charged in connection with a series of ATM bombings that occurred in Philadelphia during the unrest of June 2020. Authorities alleged that he used an explosive device to severely damage an ATM in North Philadelphia and was arrested shortly afterward while carrying additional explosives and a firearm.

He was later convicted and sentenced in June 2022 to 15 years in federal prison for using an explosive device to damage property and for illegal possession of a firearm.
profiles.finding: DOJ Philadelphia release and NYCABC support PDF match; Israeli intelligence subject unrelated.

profiles.name: John Boampong
profiles.description: On June 1, 2020 around 3 a.m., Boampong was driving near Arlington & Boylston in Boston in front of a store that had been looted that evening. After officers told him to leave, Boampong returned to the area, parked, and shot at least 11 times toward officers — including a deputized federal officer. A Sig Sauer P230 9mm with Boampong's fingerprint was recovered from his car; he was prohibited from possessing firearms due to pending state charges. Sentenced to 60 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: WBUR and Globe match Boston defendant; no accepted portrait.

profiles.name: Matthew E. Madden
profiles.description: Matthew E. Madden was arrested during protests in Kansas City, Missouri, on June 1, 2020, after police said he threw water bottles at officers and fled. A search recovered marijuana, a loaded .40-caliber pistol and an extended magazine. He entered a federal pretrial-diversion agreement, but prosecutors resumed the case after finding that he violated the agreement and absconded. Following a bench trial, he was convicted of possessing a firearm as an unlawful user of a controlled substance. The Eighth Circuit affirmed the conviction on April 25, 2025. Bureau of Prisons records list him as register number 34819-045 and in federal custody, with no projected release date published.
profiles.finding: Kansas City reporting and Eighth Circuit decision match; deceased Rhode Island and California people-search results not used.

profiles.name: Mustafah Omar Hawkins
profiles.description: In June 2020 in Cleveland, OH, Mustafah Omar Hawkins, 27, was charged with Interstate Threatening Communications after using Facebook to threaten officers. Sentenced to 2 years probation; no incarceration.
profiles.finding: Patch Bedford Heights threats report matches; no verified portrait accepted.

profiles.name: Nautica Turner
profiles.description: On June 1, 2020 Nautica Turner, 27, took lighter fluid and began pouring it on the 7-Eleven at 201 N. 17th Street in St. Louis, MO as the store was being looted. The looting was sparked by the killing of George Floyd. She pleaded guilty to a felony charge of conspiracy to commit arson. Sentenced to 27 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: KSBY sentencing report matches St Louis case; Chicago dancer and Tennessee arrest namesakes not established.

profiles.name: Preston Huteson
profiles.description: On June 1, 2020 Preston Huteson, 30, of Pasadena, CA was arrested in Compton, Los Angeles by the "Safe LA Task Force" after the George Floyd Protests. He was charged with looting; pled "no contest" to an amended count of receipt of stolen property. Sentenced to 16 months county jail; currently held in a federal California prison for other charges.
profiles.finding: Review Journal and federal Nevada case potential identity leads; require independent linkage to LA defendant.

profiles.name: Tondrique J. Fitzgerald
profiles.description: Tondrique Fitzgerald, 23, was arrested on June 1, 2020 and charged with aggravated rioting and vandalism for engaging with others to pull a granite civil rights plaque off the Historic Metro Courthouse (Nashville City Hall) wall. The plaque was smashed; pieces were used to break courthouse windows. Investigators watched Fitzgerald rip off the memorial in a Facebook Live video while encouraging others to participate. Sentenced to 48 months in Tennessee state prison.
profiles.finding: WSMV October7 2020 article explicitly captions Tondrique Fitzgerald in Nashville courthouse case, credits Metro Nashville Police Department; recognizable image visually inspected, original800x450 retained.

profiles.name: Alvin Joseph
profiles.description: Alvin Joseph is a Gwinnett County, Georgia defendant who was arrested in June 2020 on federal charges of attempted arson of police vehicles during the protests that followed the police murder of George Floyd. He was held without bond at the Robert A. Deyton Detention Facility for nearly two years pretrial. After pleading guilty to attempted arson he was sentenced on March 8, 2022. He served his sentence in the federal Bureau of Prisons and was released in summer 2025.
profiles.finding: Gwinnett Daily Post referenced by secondary report is original-source lead; Louisiana, Canadian, Navy, Dallas and officer namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Amanda R. Wolf
profiles.description: Amanda R. Wolf, age 23, of Lombard IL, was arrested June 1, 2020 and charged with attempted terrorism and possession of an incendiary device after helping co-defendant Christian Frazee approach Lombard police squad cars with a Molotov cocktail, lighters, butane torches, and a bat. Pleaded guilty; 48 months Illinois state prison.
profiles.finding: Seattle donor, Missouri alumni, Florida business and historical graves are not established Lombard subject; reject.

profiles.name: Steven M. Fitch
profiles.description: Steven M. Fitch is a Council Bluffs, Iowa resident who was found carrying a Molotov cocktail during BLM protests in downtown Omaha, Nebraska on May 31, 2020. Officers discovered in his front pants pocket a glass bottle with liquid and a red rag fuse that field-tested positive for gasoline, along with multiple lighters. The device was in operating condition and capable of exploding when ignited. Charged in the District of Nebraska, Fitch pleaded guilty to unlawful possession of a destructive device under the National Firearms Act and was sentenced to 30 months in federal prison by U.S. District Judge Brian C. Buescher.
profiles.finding: No usable portrait identified in exact-name Omaha searches; baseball player Steve Fitch unrelated.

profiles.name: Devinare Antwan Parker
profiles.description: Devinare Antwan Parker, 25, was charged in Seattle, WA with unlawful possession of a destructive device after he threw a 16-ounce can of beer through the window of a Seattle PD car, striking an officer in the face on May 31, 2020. When arrested he possessed an improvised firearm capable of firing shotgun shells. While being arrested he yelled that he had brought the firearm to kill police officers. Sentenced to 24 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: Official federal Seattle complaint corroborates case; no accepted portrait.
